The drawing shows a 4-aminoantipyrine core acylated with nicotinic acid, so the molecule is N-(1,5-dimethyl-3-oxo-2-phenylpyrazol-4-yl)nicotinamide.

**Pyrazolone ring.**
- The ring atoms are C(CH3)=C(NH...)–C(=O)–N(Ph)–N(CH3), closed back to the first carbon.
- The top carbon bears a methyl and is double-bonded to the carbon carrying the NH.
- That NH carbon is single-bonded to the C=O carbon.
- The C=O carbon is bonded to N, which carries the phenyl group.
- That N is bonded to the N that carries the N-methyl, and this N closes the ring to the methyl-bearing carbon.

**Amide and pyridine.**
- The NH is bonded to a C(=O) group, which is attached to a pyridine ring.
- The pyridine attachment carbon is adjacent to a CH that is bonded to N, so the ring is substituted at the 3-position (nicotinoyl).

**Assembled SMILES.** CC1=C(NC(=O)c2cccnc2)C(=O)N(c2ccccc2)N1C

SMILES: CC1=C(NC(=O)c2cccnc2)C(=O)N(c2ccccc2)N1C
